Main.sentence: Franklin Delano Roosevelt [a] (January 30, 1882 – April 12, 1945), also known as FDR , was the 32nd ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ from 1933 until his death in 1945. He is the longest-serving U.S. president, and the only one to have served more than two terms.

His ___E:first two terms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt_(1933%E2%80%931941))___ were centered on combating the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ , while his ___E:third and fourth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt_(1941%E2%80%931945))___ saw him shift his focus to America's involvement in ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .

A member of the prominent ___E:Delano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delano_family)___ and ___E:Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_family)___ families, Roosevelt was elected to the ___E:New York State Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Senate)___ from 1911 to 1913 and was then the ___E:assistant secretary of the Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_secretary_of_the_Navy)___ under President ___E:Woodrow Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson)___ during ___E:World War I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I)___ .

Roosevelt was ___E:James M. Cox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_M._Cox)___ 's running mate on the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ 's ticket in the ___E:1920 U.S. presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_U.S._presidential_election)___ , but Cox lost to ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ nominee ___E:Warren G. Harding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_G._Harding)___ .

In 1921, Roosevelt ___E:contracted a paralytic illness U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paralytic_illness_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ that permanently paralyzed his legs. Partly through the encouragement of his wife, ___E:Eleanor Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleanor_Roosevelt)___ , he returned to public office as ___E:governor of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_York)___ from 1929 to 1932, during which he promoted programs to combat the Great Depression.

In the ___E:1932 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1932_United_States_presidential_election)___ , Roosevelt defeated ___E:Herbert Hoover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Hoover)___ in a ___E:landslide victory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landslide_victory)___ .

During ___E:his first 100 days as president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_100_days_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt%27s_presidency)___ , Roosevelt spearheaded unprecedented federal legislation and directed the federal government during most of the Great Depression, implementing the ___E:New Deal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal)___ , building the ___E:New Deal coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Deal_coalition)___ , and realigning American politics into the ___E:Fifth Party System U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fifth_Party_System)___ .

He created numerous programs to provide relief to the unemployed and farmers while seeking economic recovery with the ___E:National Recovery Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Recovery_Administration)___ and other programs.

He also instituted major regulatory reforms related to finance, communications, and labor, and presided over the end of ___E:Prohibition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States)___ .
In 1936, Roosevelt ___E:won a landslide reelection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_United_States_presidential_election)___ .

He was unable to ___E:expand the Supreme Court in 1937 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_Procedures_Reform_Bill_of_1937)___ , the same year the ___E:conservative coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_coalition)___ was formed to block the implementation of further New Deal programs and reforms.

Major surviving programs and legislation implemented under Roosevelt include the ___E:Securities and Exchange Commission U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_and_Exchange_Commission)___ , the ___E:National Labor Relations Act U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Labor_Relations_Act_of_1935)___ , the ___E:Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Deposit_Insurance_Corporation)___ , and ___E:Social Security U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Security_(United_States))___ .

In ___E:1940 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1940_United_States_presidential_election)___ , he ___E:ran successfully for reelection U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1940_United_States_presidential_election)___ , before the ___E:official implementation of term limits U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-second_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution)___ .

Following the Japanese ___E:attack on Pearl Harbor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor)___ on December 7, 1941, Roosevelt obtained a declaration of war on ___E:Japan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan)___ .

When in turn, Japan's Axis partners, ___E:Nazi Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany)___ and ___E:Fascist Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascist_Italy)___ , declared war on the U.S. on December 11, 1941, he secured additional declarations of war from the ___E:United States Congress U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress)___ .

He worked closely with other national leaders in leading the ___E:Allies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II)___ against the ___E:Axis powers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers)___ .
Roosevelt supervised the mobilization of the American economy to support the war effort and implemented a ___E:Europe first U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Europe_first)___ strategy.

He also initiated the development of the first atomic bomb and worked with the other Allied leaders to lay the groundwork for the ___E:United Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_Nations)___ and other post-war institutions, even coining the term "United Nations".

Roosevelt ___E:won reelection in 1944 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1944_United_States_presidential_election)___ , but died in 1945 after his physical health seriously and steadily declined during the war years.

Since then, several of his actions have come under ___E:criticism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criticism_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ , such as his ordering of the ___E:internment of Japanese Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internment_of_Japanese_Americans)___ .

Nonetheless, ___E:historical rankings U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States)___ consistently place him among the three greatest American presidents, and he is often considered an icon of ___E:American liberalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberalism_in_the_United_States)___ .

Franklin Delano Roosevelt was born on January 30, 1882, in ___E:Hyde Park, New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_New_York)___ , to businessman ___E:James Roosevelt I U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Roosevelt_I)___ and his second wife, ___E:Sara Ann Delano U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Ann_Delano)___ .

His parents, who were sixth cousins,  came from wealthy, established New York families—the ___E:Roosevelts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roosevelt_family)___ and the ___E:Delanos U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delano_family)___ , respectively—and resided at ___E:Springwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt_National_Historic_Site)___ , a large estate south of Hyde Park's historic center.

James was a prominent ___E:Bourbon Democrat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourbon_Democrat)___ who once took Franklin to meet President ___E:Grover Cleveland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover_Cleveland)___ .

During this meeting, Cleveland said: "My little man, I am making a strange wish for you. It is that you may never be President of the United States."  Franklin's mother Sara, the dominant influence in his early years, once declared, "My son Franklin is a Delano, not a Roosevelt at all."   James, who was 54 when Franklin was born, was considered by some as a remote father, though biographer ___E:James MacGregor Burns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_MacGregor_Burns)___ indicates James interacted with his son more than was typical at the time.  Franklin had a half-brother, ___E:James Roosevelt "Rosy" Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Roosevelt_Roosevelt)___ , from his father's previous marriage.

As a child, Roosevelt learned to ride, shoot, sail, and play polo, tennis, and golf.   Frequent trips to Europe—beginning at age two and from age seven to fifteen—helped Roosevelt become ___E:conversant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_multilingual_presidents_of_the_United_States)___ in German and French.

Except for attending public school in Germany at age nine,  Roosevelt was ___E:homeschooled U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeschooling)___ by tutors until age 14. He then attended ___E:Groton School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groton_School)___ , an Episcopal boarding school in ___E:Groton, Massachusetts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groton,_Massachusetts)___ .
He was not among the more popular Groton students, who were better athletes and had rebellious streaks.

Its headmaster, ___E:Endicott Peabody U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endicott_Peabody_(educator))___ , preached the duty of Christians to help the less fortunate and urged his students to enter public service.
Peabody remained a strong influence throughout Roosevelt's life, officiating at his wedding and visiting him as president.
Like most of his Groton classmates, Roosevelt went to ___E:Harvard College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_College)___ .

He was a member of the ___E:Alpha Delta Phi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_Delta_Phi)___ fraternity  and the ___E:Fly Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly_Club)___ ,  and served as a school cheerleader.

Roosevelt was relatively undistinguished as a student or athlete, but he became editor-in-chief of The Harvard Crimson daily newspaper, which required ambition, energy, and the ability to manage others.
He later said, "I took economics courses in college for four years, and everything I was taught was wrong."
Roosevelt's father died in 1900, distressing him greatly.
The following year, Roosevelt's fifth cousin ___E:Theodore Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt)___ became U.S. president.

Theodore's vigorous leadership style and reforming zeal made him Franklin's role model and hero.  He graduated from Harvard in three years in 1903 with an ___E:A.B. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts)___ in history.
He remained there for a fourth year, taking graduate courses.
Like his cousin Theodore, he was a member of ___E:The Explorers Club U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Explorers_Club)___ .

Roosevelt entered ___E:Columbia Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Law_School)___ in 1904, but dropped out in 1907 after passing the ___E:New York bar examination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_examination_in_the_United_States)___ .  [b] In 1908, he took a job with the prestigious ___E:law firm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_firm)___ of ___E:Carter Ledyard & Milburn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carter_Ledyard_%26_Milburn)___ , working in the firm's ___E:admiralty law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiralty_law)___ division.

Roosevelt was an avid ___E:stamp collector U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamp_collector)___ who came into the hobby beginning at eight years old, and continued this pursuit into his adulthood and political career.
During his terms as president he aroused nationwide interest in stamp collecting.
Beginning in the 1930s, the White House released numerous photographs of him while he was attending his stamp collection.
He devoted time each day working with his collection.
He worked with Postmaster General ___E:James A. Farley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_A._Farley)___ over stamp designs, colors, and themes for U.S. postage stamps.
When he became stricken with polio it is said the hobby gave him solace and kept his mind off his ailments during his idle hours.

During his second year of college, Roosevelt met and proposed to Boston heiress Alice Sohier, who turned him down.  Franklin then began courting his childhood acquaintance and fifth cousin once removed, ___E:Eleanor Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleanor_Roosevelt)___ , a niece of Theodore Roosevelt.
In 1903, Franklin proposed to Eleanor.

Despite resistance from his mother, Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt were married on March 17, 1905.   Eleanor's father, ___E:Elliott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_B._Roosevelt)___ , was deceased; Theodore, who was then president, gave away the bride.
The young couple moved into ___E:Springwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_of_Franklin_D._Roosevelt_National_Historic_Site)___ .
Franklin's mother, Sara Roosevelt, also provided a townhouse for the newlyweds in New York City, and had a house built for herself alongside that townhouse.

Eleanor never felt at home in the houses at Hyde Park or New York City; however, she loved the family's vacation home on ___E:Campobello Island U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campobello_Island)___ , which was also a gift from Sara.
Burns indicates that young Franklin Roosevelt was self-assured and at ease in the upper class.
On the other hand, Eleanor was shy and disliked social life. Initially, Eleanor stayed home to raise their children.
As his father had done, Franklin left childcare to his wife, and Eleanor delegated the task to caregivers.
She later said that she knew "absolutely nothing about handling or feeding a baby".

They had six children. ___E:Anna U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Roosevelt_Halsted)___ , ___E:James U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Roosevelt)___ , and ___E:Elliott U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliott_Roosevelt_(general))___ were born in 1906, 1907, and 1910, respectively.

The couple's second son, Franklin, died in infancy in 1909. Another son, also named ___E:Franklin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_Delano_Roosevelt_Jr.)___ , was born in 1914, and the youngest, ___E:John U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Aspinwall_Roosevelt)___ , was born in 1916.
Roosevelt had several extramarital affairs.

He commenced an affair with Eleanor's social secretary, ___E:Lucy Mercer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucy_Mercer)___ , soon after she was hired in 1914. That affair was discovered by Eleanor in 1918.  Franklin contemplated divorcing Eleanor, but Sara objected, and Mercer would not marry a divorced man with five children.
Franklin and Eleanor remained married, and Franklin promised never to see Mercer again.
Eleanor never forgave him for the affair, and their marriage shifted to become a political partnership.
Eleanor soon established a separate home in Hyde Park at ___E:Val-Kill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Val-Kill)___ and devoted herself to social and political causes independent of her husband.
The emotional break in their marriage was so severe that when Franklin asked Eleanor in 1942—in light of his failing health—to come live with him again, she refused.
Roosevelt was not always aware of Eleanor's visits to the White House.
For some time, Eleanor could not easily reach Roosevelt on the telephone without his secretary's help; Franklin, in turn, did not visit Eleanor's New York City apartment until late 1944.
Franklin broke his promise to Eleanor regarding Lucy Mercer.

He and Mercer maintained a formal correspondence and began seeing each other again by 1941.   Roosevelt's son Elliott claimed that his father had a 20-year affair with his private secretary, ___E:Marguerite LeHand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marguerite_LeHand)___ .

Another son, James, stated that "there is a real possibility that a romantic relationship existed" between his father and ___E:Crown Princess Märtha of Norway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_Princess_M%C3%A4rtha_of_Norway)___ , who resided in the White House during part of World War II. Aides referred to her at the time as "the president's girlfriend",  and gossip linking the two romantically appeared in newspapers.
Roosevelt cared little for the practice of law and told friends he planned to enter politics.

Despite his admiration for cousin Theodore, Franklin shared his father's bond with the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ , and in preparation for the ___E:1910 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1910_New_York_state_election)___ , the party recruited Roosevelt to run for a seat in the ___E:New York State Assembly U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Assembly)___ .
Roosevelt was a compelling recruit: he had the personality and energy for campaigning and the money to pay for his own campaign.

But Roosevelt's campaign for the state assembly ended after the Democratic incumbent, ___E:Lewis Stuyvesant Chanler U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Stuyvesant_Chanler)___ , chose to seek re-election.
Rather than putting his political hopes on hold, Roosevelt ran for a seat in the ___E:New York State Senate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Senate)___ .

The senate district, located in ___E:Dutchess U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutchess_County,_New_York)___ , ___E:Columbia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_County,_New_York)___ , and ___E:Putnam Counties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Putnam_County,_New_York)___ , was strongly Republican.
Roosevelt feared that opposition from Theodore could end his campaign, but Theodore encouraged his candidacy despite their party differences.

Acting as his own campaign manager, Roosevelt traveled throughout the senate district via automobile at a time when few could afford a car.  Due to his aggressive campaign,  his name gained recognition in the ___E:Hudson Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_Valley)___ , and in the Democratic landslide in the ___E:1910 United States elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1910_United_States_elections)___ , Roosevelt won a surprising victory.
Despite short legislative sessions, Roosevelt treated his new position as a full-time career.

Taking his seat on January 1, 1911, Roosevelt soon became the leader of a group of "Insurgents" in opposition to the ___E:Tammany Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tammany_Hall)___ machine that dominated the state Democratic Party.

In the ___E:1911 U.S. Senate election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1911_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_York)___ , which was determined in a joint session of the New York state legislature, [c] Roosevelt and nineteen other Democrats caused a prolonged deadlock by opposing a series of Tammany-backed candidates.

Tammany threw its backing behind ___E:James A. O'Gorman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_A._O%27Gorman)___ , a highly regarded judge whom Roosevelt found acceptable, and O'Gorman won the election in late March.
Roosevelt in the process became a popular figure among New York Democrats.
News articles and cartoons depicted "the second coming of a Roosevelt", sending "cold shivers down the spine of Tammany".

Shortly after being elected to the New York State Senate, Roosevelt became a ___E:Freemason U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freemasonry)___ , on October 10, 1911, at Holland Lodge No. 8 in New York City.

Roosevelt also opposed Tammany Hall by supporting New Jersey Governor ___E:Woodrow Wilson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson)___ 's successful bid for the ___E:1912 Democratic nomination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_Democratic_National_Convention)___ .

The election became a three-way contest when Theodore Roosevelt left the Republican Party to launch a third-party campaign against Wilson and sitting Republican president ___E:William Howard Taft U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft)___ .

Franklin's decision to back Wilson over his cousin in the ___E:general election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_United_States_presidential_election)___ alienated some of his family, except Theodore.

Roosevelt overcame a bout of ___E:typhoid fever U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoid_fever)___ that year and, with help from journalist ___E:Louis McHenry Howe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_McHenry_Howe)___ , he was re-elected in the ___E:1912 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_New_York_state_election)___ .
After the election, he served as chairman of the Agriculture Committee; his success with farm and labor bills was a precursor to his later New Deal policies.
He had then become more consistently ___E:progressive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Era)___ , in support of labor and social welfare programs.

Roosevelt's support of Wilson led to his appointment in March 1913 as ___E:Assistant Secretary of the Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_of_the_Navy)___ , the second-ranking official in the ___E:Navy Department U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ after Secretary ___E:Josephus Daniels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josephus_Daniels)___ who paid it little attention.
Roosevelt had an affection for the ___E:Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ , was well-read on the subject, and was an ardent supporter of a large, efficient force.

With Wilson's support, Daniels and Roosevelt instituted a merit-based promotion system and extended civilian control over the autonomous departments of the Navy.  Roosevelt oversaw the Navy's civilian employees and earned the respect of union leaders for his fairness in resolving disputes.
No strikes occurred during his seven-plus years in the office,  as he gained valuable experience in labor issues, wartime management, naval issues, and logistics.

In 1914, Roosevelt ran for the seat of retiring Republican Senator ___E:Elihu Root U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_Root)___ of New York. Though he had the backing of Treasury Secretary ___E:William Gibbs McAdoo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Gibbs_McAdoo)___ and Governor ___E:Martin H. Glynn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_H._Glynn)___ , he faced a formidable opponent in Tammany Hall's ___E:James W. Gerard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_W._Gerard)___ .
He also was without Wilson's support, as the president needed Tammany's forces for his legislation and 1916 re-election.

Roosevelt was soundly defeated in the Democratic primary by Gerard, who in turn lost the general election to Republican ___E:James Wolcott Wadsworth Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Wolcott_Wadsworth_Jr.)___ He learned that federal patronage alone, without White House support, could not defeat a strong local organization.
After the election, he and Tammany Hall boss ___E:Charles Francis Murphy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Francis_Murphy)___ sought accommodation and became allies.

Roosevelt refocused on the Navy Department as World War I broke out in Europe in August 1914.  Though he remained publicly supportive of Wilson, Roosevelt sympathized with the ___E:Preparedness Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preparedness_Movement)___ , whose leaders strongly favored the Allied Powers and called for a military build-up.  The Wilson administration initiated an expansion of the Navy after the ___E:sinking of the RMS Lusitania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinking_of_the_RMS_Lusitania)___ by a German ___E:submarine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine)___ , and Roosevelt helped establish the ___E:United States Navy Reserve U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Reserve)___ and the ___E:Council of National Defense U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_National_Defense)___ .

In April 1917, after Germany declared it would engage in ___E:unrestricted submarine warfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unrestricted_submarine_warfare)___ and attacked several U.S. ships, Congress approved Wilson's call for a ___E:declaration of war on Germany U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_declaration_of_war_on_Germany_(1917))___ .
Roosevelt requested that he be allowed to serve as a naval officer, but Wilson insisted that he continue as Assistant Secretary.
For the next year, Roosevelt remained in Washington to coordinate the naval deployment, as the Navy expanded fourfold.
In the summer of 1918, Roosevelt traveled to Europe to inspect naval installations and meet with French and British officials.

On account of his relation to Theodore Roosevelt, he was received very prominently considering his relatively junior rank, obtaining long private audiences with King ___E:George V U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_V)___ and prime ministers ___E:David Lloyd George U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Lloyd_George)___ and ___E:Georges Clemenceau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georges_Clemenceau)___ , as well as a tour of the ___E:battlefield at Verdun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Verdun)___ .

In September, on the ship voyage back to the United States, he contracted ___E:pandemic influenza U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1918_flu_pandemic)___ with complicating pneumonia,  which left him unable to work for a month.

After Germany signed an ___E:armistice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice_of_11_November_1918)___ in November 1918, Daniels and Roosevelt supervised the demobilization of the Navy.  Against the advice of older officers such as Admiral ___E:William S. Benson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_S._Benson)___ —who claimed he could not "conceive of any use the fleet will ever have for aviation"—Roosevelt personally ordered the preservation of the Navy's ___E:Aviation Division U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Aeronautics#Origins:_1920s_and_1930s)___ .
With the Wilson administration near an end, Roosevelt planned his next run for office.
He approached ___E:Herbert Hoover U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Hoover)___ about running for the 1920 Democratic presidential nomination, with Roosevelt as his running mate.

Roosevelt's plan for Hoover to run fell through after Hoover publicly declared himself to be a Republican, but Roosevelt decided to seek the 1920 ___E:vice presidential U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States)___ nomination.

After Governor ___E:James M. Cox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_M._Cox)___ of Ohio won the party's presidential nomination at the ___E:1920 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_Democratic_National_Convention)___ , he chose Roosevelt as his running mate, and the convention nominated him by ___E:acclamation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acclamation)___ .

Although his nomination surprised most people, he balanced the ticket as a moderate, a Wilsonian, and a ___E:prohibitionist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition_in_the_United_States)___ with a famous name.   Roosevelt, then 38, resigned as Assistant Secretary after the Democratic convention and campaigned across the nation for the party ticket.

During the campaign, Cox and Roosevelt defended the Wilson administration and the ___E:League of Nations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations)___ , both of which were unpopular in 1920.  Roosevelt personally supported U.S. membership in the League, but, unlike Wilson, he favored compromising with Senator ___E:Henry Cabot Lodge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cabot_Lodge)___ and other "Reservationists".

Republicans ___E:Warren G. Harding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_G._Harding)___ and ___E:Calvin Coolidge U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Coolidge)___ defeated the Cox–Roosevelt ticket in the ___E:presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1920_United_States_presidential_election)___ by a wide margin, carrying every state outside of the South.
Roosevelt accepted the loss and later reflected that the relationships and goodwill that he built in the 1920 campaign proved to be a major asset in his 1932 campaign.

The 1920 election also saw the first public participation of Eleanor Roosevelt who, with the support of ___E:Louis Howe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Howe)___ , established herself as a valuable political player.

After the election, Roosevelt returned to New York City, where he practiced law and served as a vice president of the ___E:Fidelity and Deposit Company U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidelity_and_Deposit_Company)___ .
Roosevelt sought to build support for a political comeback in the ___E:1922 elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_elections,_1922)___ , but his career was derailed by an illness.
